name: RxnOptBench
description: A frozen evaluation-only benchmark of 4,773 constructed reaction-condition QA records in eight test subsets, derived from human-reviewed published screening tables. Source experimental measurements are literature-derived. MC and FIB subsets expose different observed candidate supports; archived utility and dr/rr target-direction limitations are documented in the RAI fields and dataset card. Each Croissant record exposes its full original JSON record as lossless UTF-8 Text (json_record) in a derived gzipped TSV, plus searchable identifiers. Decode json_record with a JSON parser to recover nested inputs, candidates, answers, and provenance; record_schema.json documents all nested fields. Identifiers are unique within their subset, not across all eight subsets.
conditionsOfAccess: Data are licensed under the RxnOptBench Noncommercial Research License v1.0. Download requires a Hugging Face account and acceptance of a lightweight noncommercial research-use agreement; approval is automatic after acceptance. Metadata and MIT evaluation code are publicly available at https://github.com/SII-gelingli/RxnOptBench. The provided load/validation script uses an authorized cached Hugging Face login or HF_TOKEN to download and hash-check transport files, then supplies them to mlcroissant using its standard local mapping API. The reference loader itself does not read HF_TOKEN for arbitrary HTTP FileObjects. Acceptance of the access agreement is still required.

rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark measures selection among candidates derived from disclosed literature screening tables. A best answer is best within a question's observed-row support under the declared utility; it is not a global optimum over chemical space. The release is not validated for direct wet-lab guidance, autonomous experimentation, safety or cost assessment, or open-ended synthesis planning.

Fill-in-the-blank candidate values are individually source-derived, but their Cartesian product contains unobserved joint tuples. A structurally valid tuple that does not match an observed source-table row is a non-Hit outside measured support, not a chemically invalid reaction or a measured failure. Score conditioned on Hit excludes these unobserved tuples.

The frozen headline utility includes archived parsed dr/rr factors normalized row by row toward major:minor. This can discard target-isomer identity. Numeric product labels inside ratio strings also require careful parsing. Complete target-aware re-adjudication of every archived label has not been established; this release must not be described as fully target-aware relabelled data. The paper separately discloses a dr/rr-removal sensitivity audit and a maintenance parser correction.

The public evaluators deterministically score supplied predictions on the frozen test files. This does not reproduce historical model generations or establish invariance across hosted model endpoints, backend updates, decoding configurations, or time. Frozen reported paper aggregates and later scoring or repeated-call audits are distinct results.

The paper's source sampling frame is papers first published in 2025 across 16 selected journals. Expert verification checked extracted chemical records against source PDFs. This temporal restriction reduces but does not eliminate training contamination; model training cutoffs and source exposure are not fully observable.

This release contains only the final human-reviewed test set, deterministic evaluators, and minimal usage examples and documentation. It does not include raw publisher documents or images, the extraction or question-construction pipeline, review tooling, inference runners, or archived model outputs. It therefore supports fixed-test-set evaluation rather than reconstruction from raw PDFs.

Frozen meta.doi fields are source-identifier strings, not a normalized DOI registry. The MC-all file contains 552 parent-table identifiers and 236 case-sensitive raw source strings; four case-variant groups reduce this to 232 case-insensitive identifiers, matching the paper's article count. This identifier audit does not newly resolve every identifier through a DOI registry or establish publisher permissions. Frozen source strings are retained.
rai:dataBiases: Publication and narrative-selection bias affect which experiments are disclosed: methodology tables are curated evidence supporting a paper rather than complete optimization histories. Successful, interesting, and publishable transformations and selected comparison rows may be overrepresented. The benchmark uses the disclosed rows' reported outcomes and does not claim to recover undisclosed experimental histories.

Venue selection, the 2025 sampling frame, extraction feasibility, and human curation create uneven coverage of reaction classes, substrate families, catalysts, condition fields, and table formats. Tables that cannot be reliably structured or lack usable reaction or outcome information are underrepresented.

Paired precedent tasks programmatically select and expose lower- or middle-performing observed rows while withholding best rows. This constructed context distribution is part of the task design and need not match the information available to a chemist conducting an experiment.

Relative aggregate utility emphasizes reported yield and available stereoselectivity terms. Missing selectivity factors, archived major:minor dr/rr normalization, parsing choices, and source reporting conventions can affect labels and answer rankings. The utility does not represent every chemical objective, preferred target isomer, safety constraint, or cost preference.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The test records describe chemical reactions, conditions, reported outcomes, and source identifiers. No personal, demographic, medical, political, or other human-sensitive attributes are intentionally collected as benchmark features. Public author and maintainer information appears in dataset documentation. The paper reports only aggregate information about six paid chemistry interns who performed verification; individual annotator identities are not released as test-set attributes.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended use: offline testing and comparison of reaction-condition recommendation systems on a fixed, source-derived candidate space, including single-axis versus joint-condition selection and precedent versus no-precedent ablations. Report MC Accuracy and relative Score, and distinguish FIB observed-row Hit, Strict Accuracy, and Score conditioned on Hit.

The construct is comparative selection of better disclosed conditions for the same reaction, supported by human-verified matched source-table rows with experimentally reported outcomes. It is conditional on the disclosed candidates and the declared utility, not a measure of unrestricted optimization ability or laboratory readiness.

The provided split is test-only. Training or fine-tuning on these records compromises evaluation on the same questions; no disjoint training/validation split or established fine-tuning benefit is provided. Direct wet-lab deployment, autonomous experimentation, safety certification, and inference of outcomes for unobserved condition tuples have not been validated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The release can support reproducible comparison and diagnosis of chemistry AI systems. Machine-readable aggregation also lowers the effort needed to find and reuse published condition information, creating misuse risk and a risk that offline benchmark scores are mistaken for experimental readiness. Documentation retains source provenance, distinguishes unobserved tuples from measured failures, explains scoring and sampling limitations, and directs users to qualified expert review and independent validation before any experimental use. The selected data policy is the custom RxnOptBench Noncommercial Research License v1.0, with a lightweight research-use download agreement and automatic approval after acceptance. The code uses MIT. The agreement provides accountability and friction rather than proof of safe use or legal clearance.
rai:dataCollection: The paper describes manual acquisition of source papers and supporting information through open-access channels or university institutional subscriptions, with local processing and no automated bulk crawling of publisher websites. Its sampling frame is papers first published in 2025. A four-stage semi-automated workflow detects and structures condition-screening tables using visual-language-model extraction and deterministic checks, followed by human verification of each retained table against its source. Reported experimental outcomes are not simulated or newly generated. The hasSyntheticData flag is conservatively true for the programmatically constructed QA layer, including candidate arrangement, masking, reference/control contexts, and computed answer/relative-score annotations; it does not describe the underlying chemical measurements as synthetic.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Four master's-level and two doctoral-level paid chemistry interns based in mainland China reviewed extracted tables against source PDFs, corrected structured fields, and accepted, rejected, or skipped tables through an internal review interface. Only accepted records entered question construction. The paper reports compensation of RMB 300 per working day for the four master's-level interns and RMB 400 per working day for the two doctoral-level interns. The release makes no claim of independent multiple labels per item or a measured inter-annotator-agreement statistic. Questions and answer sets were subsequently constructed from the reviewed rows under the declared candidate-space and utility rules.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Internal per-table expert-review interface described in the paper. The interface implementation and individual review logs are outside this evaluation-only release.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Programmatic transformations form single-axis and whole-row MC tasks and per-axis-index FIB tasks from reviewed observations, shuffle candidate orders, and form matched precedent/control variants. No additional measured yields or stereoselectivities are invented. FIB exposes recombinations in the prediction space but supplies outcome scores only for observed joint rows. The frozen 0.2.5-eval-only candidate indices and labels are preserved. JSONL files are transport representations of the corresponding native JSON test files. Archived dr/rr normalization and parsing limitations are disclosed in dataLimitations rather than silently presented as resolved.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Version 0.2.5-eval-only is a frozen evaluation snapshot. Corrections should be documented in a versioned release with candidate-index and scoring changes distinguished from unchanged historical paper aggregates. Report dataset, provenance, scoring, misuse, or rights concerns to Conghui He at heconghui@pjlab.org.cn, or use the linked GitHub repository issue tracker. Code uses MIT; data uses the custom RxnOptBench Noncommercial Research License v1.0. No maintenance schedule or service guarantee is asserted here.

prov:wasDerivedFrom.sc:name: Published organic-methodology screening tables described in the RxnOptBench paper
prov:wasDerivedFrom.sc:description: This URI identifies the release documentation of the upstream literature sources, not a separately hosted normalized source dataset. Raw source identifiers and table/row back-pointers are retained in meta.doi, meta.parent_table_id, meta.source_file, and option_source_entries or legal_combinations in the eight native files under data/original_json/. The release does not claim that these raw strings constitute a reconciled DOI registry or redistribute publisher PDFs.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:name: Literature selection and structured extraction
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Manual source acquisition; local visual-language-model-assisted detection and extraction; deterministic normalization and structural checks. The paper describes 911 candidate tables, 552 retained tables, and 5,451 reviewed row-level reaction records. Acquisition dates, model prompts, and pipeline implementation are not newly invented or included by this metadata patch.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:name: Human verification and question construction
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Six compensated chemistry interns compared extracted records with source PDFs and edited, accepted, rejected, or skipped tables. Accepted rows were transformed into MC/FIB questions, reference and control variants, and frozen answer and score annotations. Synthetic content is limited to this constructed task layer; source experimental measurements remain literature-derived. The archived utility's dr/rr target-direction limitations remain disclosed.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:name: Evaluation-only camera-ready packaging
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Preserve the 0.2.5-eval-only human-reviewed test files and matching candidate indices; provide eight JSONL subsets, eight native JSON files, two deterministic evaluation scripts, minimal prediction-schema examples, and documentation. No extraction pipeline, model outputs, publisher documents, or source images are part of the release. Include MIT code terms and the custom RxnOptBench Noncommercial Research License v1.0 data terms. Core Croissant metadata documents the lossless transport, and loader/access verification is recorded separately in validation reports.
